# Speed Matrix results - current grid below from full run 30791970390 (2026-08-03, the first grid with JIT genuinely off: runs before workflow fix 12f093e inherited the runner's JIT-on ini while labeled off. No verdict changes except thresh-64 - Linux now wins the 64-127B band, adopted below). Earlier runs (all effectively JIT-on): full 29868666232 (2026-07-21, corpus-density pools) and 29670857386/29675354782/29676033393 (2026-07-18/19); filtered 29690005430 and 29690465062 (thresh-128-*/strtr-* and thresh-64/os/arch rows), 29715636255 (cast-* rows), 29866984899 (stack-accented-short and arr-get-method/arr-foreach rows); jit=tracing confirmation 29864749405.

Note: the workflow's `filter` input takes exact test ids, comma-separated
(`-f filter=cast-int,cast-guard-short`) - prefixes match nothing.

Run: https://github.com/interactivetools-com/SmartString/actions/runs/30791970390
(25 cells: PHP 8.1-8.5 x linux-x64/linux-arm/windows-x64/macos-x64/macos-arm,
scale=1.0, JIT off). Generated by speed-probe.php per cell, merged by
speed-merge.php; see speed-probe.php for what each test measures.

To regenerate: dispatch the Speed Matrix workflow (Actions tab or
`gh workflow run speed-matrix.yml`), download the probe-* artifacts, then
`php speed-merge.php probes/*.json`.

Pool densities match measured corpus rates (see the note atop the pools
region in speed-probe.php): accented1k carries ~2.5-3% accented characters
(French prose density), the mix's 5% specials share is prose1k (one quoted
phrase plus two apostrophes per KB, typed-content density), and dirty10's
special is an apostrophe. The grid below is measured on these pools.

Verdicts from this run (details in the per-test rows below):

### Adopted

- **gate-preg** (identity fast path): SmartString 3.0 - see ENCODE_SKIP_REGEX in
  src/SmartString.php. Positive on all 25 cells.
- **arr-get** (folded __get): SmartArray 3.0 - see __get() in
  src/SmartArrayBase.php; union return kept (arr-get-mixed gain does not
  reproduce cross-platform).
- **prop-type**: SmartString 3.0 - $rawData is untyped (typed ctor param +
  ImmutabilityTest cover the contract); see its docblock.
- **tier-strrep + gate-unicode** (the three-tier stack): SmartString 3.0 - see
  the ENCODE_SKIP_REGEX docblock in src/SmartString.php. Adopted ungated on all
  platforms: realistic mix 3.3-7.1x baseline on Linux/macOS (Linux ARM mildest),
  8.1-9.3x Windows (stack-mix); accented text 3.1-10.8x (stack-accented-mix).
  Bounded losses: short fields containing specials pay ~16-127ns extra
  (stack-miss-short; macOS ARM mildest, ~270ns worst on macOS x64);
  short accented fields ~73-182ns on Linux, ~36-81ns on macOS ARM, ~65-126ns on
  Windows (stack-accented-short; all three scans miss or reach tier 3; one
  1KB accented win repays ~30 of them); invalid UTF-8 ~even (stack-invalid-1kb).
- **gate-hybrid-len** (adopted 2026-07-19): tier 1 routes long strings to strspn
  on PHP 8.4+ (`PHP_VERSION_ID >= 80400 && strlen >= ENCODE_STRSPN_MIN_BYTES`);
  see ENCODE_CLEAN_CHARS in src/SmartString.php. On 8.1-8.3 every cell is an
  exact tie - the version branch provably compiles away (and elseif vs nested
  else compile identically, verified via opcache opt_debug_level dump). On 8.4+:
  1.5-2.3x on 1KB clean, ~even to +11% on the realistic mix, 0.90-0.99x on shorts
  (the strlen guard, ~1-3ns - strlen reads the stored length, it never scans).
  scan-cross-* locates the preg/strspn crossover: 64B on linux-x64/linux-arm/
  windows (darwin-x64 borderline), ~128B on darwin-arm.
  Corpus covers the 63/64/65, 127/128/129, and 255/256/257 boundaries;
  EncodingCorpusTest also proves ENCODE_CLEAN_CHARS is the exact byte
  complement of ENCODE_SKIP_REGEX.
- **thresh-128** (adopted 2026-07-19, run 29690005430): ENCODE_STRSPN_MIN_BYTES
  lowered 256 -> 128. Every 8.4+ cell wins on the 128-255B band (1.06-1.39x at
  128B, 1.11-1.61x at 200B); every 8.1-8.3 cell is an exact tie (dead branch).
- **thresh-os** (adopted 2026-07-19, run 29690465062; superseded 2026-08-03 by
  thresh-64 Linux below): gave Windows the 64B minimum while everything else
  stayed at 128. Windows PHP builds are x64-only (no ARM64 builds exist), so
  the OS check implies the architecture.
- **thresh-64 Linux** (adopted 2026-08-03, run 30791970390):
  ENCODE_STRSPN_MIN_BYTES is 128 on Darwin, 64 everywhere else. The first true
  JIT-off grid flipped Linux: 64-127B clean strings win 1.05-1.20x on
  linux-x64/linux-arm 8.4+ (thresh-64-64b/96b; scan-cross-64 agrees at
  1.07-1.12x) where the JIT-on grids measured 0.92-0.93x losses - JIT was
  cutting the preg gate's per-call overhead, and production PHP runs JIT off.
  darwin-arm still loses at 64B (0.92-0.93x), so Darwin keeps 128; BSD and
  Solaris are unmeasured and take the Linux value. Every 8.1-8.3 cell stays a
  dead-branch tie.
- **cast fast path** (adopted 2026-07-19, confirmed run 29715636255): non-string
  rawData (int/float/bool/null) returns (string)$value with no scan in
  __toString()/htmlEncode(). cast-int wins all 25 cells, 1.76-2.37x.
  cast-guard-short (the is_string check's cost on the
  string path) reads as a tie: 0.85-1.02x scattered around 1.00 with no
  platform pattern - a few ns on a ~40ns operation, repaid ~2x on every
  non-string value.

### Rejected

- **gate-adaptive** (strspn on 8.4+): loses on short strings on every platform,
  including 8.4+.
- **promo**: tie everywhere - constructor promotion is pure style, settled.
- **memo-mix**: tie-to-slower everywhere - memo cache is pure overhead.
- **strtr** (rejected 2026-07-19, run 29690005430): single-pass strtr in tiers
  2-3 vs the 5-pass str_replace. Sparse 1KB (one special) loses on all 25 cells
  (0.61-0.91x); dense 1KB loses on all Linux cells (0.62-0.94x) with only
  scattered wins (darwin-arm <= 8.4, windows 8.1); short dirty is a small
  inconsistent win (0.95-1.22x). Matches the C source: str_replace's per-needle
  count scans are SSE2-vectorized and absent needles are zero-copy, while
  php_strtr_array_ex pays a per-call bitset alloc sized to the input plus a
  scalar byte loop. Settled with data - do not re-open without new C-level
  changes in php-src.
- **thresh-64 flat** (rejected 2026-07-19; re-checked JIT-off 2026-08-03, run
  30791970390): 64B minimum on all platforms still loses on darwin-arm
  (0.92-0.93x at 8.4+). The linux-x64 loss in the JIT-on grids did not survive
  JIT-off measurement - see thresh-64 Linux above. Platform-split, not flat.
- **thresh-arch** (rejected 2026-07-19, run 29690465062): the 64B threshold for
  Windows plus Linux ARM needs php_uname('m'), a function call - illegal in
  constant expressions, so it must be a runtime define() that opcache cannot
  fold. The per-call constant fetch is not reliably free: cells that should tie
  showed 0.85-0.94x (thresh-arch-64b darwin-x64 8.4, thresh-arch-short
  linux-x64 8.5). Moot since thresh-64 Linux: every 64B winner is now
  detectable from PHP_OS_FAMILY alone, no architecture check needed.

### Measured for reference (no code change)

- **stack-mix / stack-accented-mix**: the full three-tier stack vs plain
  htmlspecialchars - realistic mix 3.3-3.5x Linux ARM, 3.9-7.1x elsewhere,
  8.1-9.3x Windows (vs 1.8-2.7x for the gate alone); accented mix 3.1-10.8x.
- **idiom**: ->htmlEncode() is a few percent faster than (string) cast - a
  docs tip, not a code change.
- **specials-content break-even vs the helper** (interpolated from JIT-off
  Speed Page Table run 30791972198): on fields containing specials, SmartString
  pulls ahead of the plain htmlspecialchars helper above ~90B on linux-x64,
  ~115B on linux-arm, ~25B on windows. Density- and platform-dependent; add
  64B/256B specials rows if it ever needs pinning.
- **jit=tracing confirmation** (run 29864749405, 2026-07-21): all 25 cells with
  opcache JIT tracing - same verdicts as the JIT-off grid below except
  thresh-64: JIT trims the preg gate's per-call overhead enough to flip the
  64-127B band against strspn on Linux (see thresh-64 Linux above). The
  JIT-off grid remains the citable source - production PHP runs JIT off.
- **arr-get-method**: `->key` (folded __get) beats
  `->get('key')` (the 4-call chain) 1.12-1.65x on 24 of 25 cells (one tie,
  linux-x64 8.2). Docs angle:
  property access is both the recommended and the fast form; a get() fold
  would narrow the gap (queued in SmartArray's todo).
- **arr-foreach**: returning ArrayIterator($data) from
  getIterator() instead of the per-element generator wins 1.24-1.65x on all
  25 cells for a foreach pass over a 64-row list (rows are nested arrays,
  so the generator's wrap check never fires). Adoption candidate queued in
  SmartArray's todo.

<details><summary>Test legend (A vs B)</summary>

- **promo**: manual assignment vs ctor promotion
- **prop-type**: typed readonly prop vs untyped prop (typed ctor)
- **gate-preg-short**: htmlspecialchars vs preg identity gate
- **gate-preg-1kb**: htmlspecialchars vs preg identity gate
- **gate-preg-mix**: htmlspecialchars vs preg identity gate
- **gate-miss-short**: htmlspecialchars vs gate (always misses)
- **gate-miss-1kb**: htmlspecialchars vs gate (always misses)
- **strspn-cliff**: preg gate scan vs strspn scan
- **gate-adaptive-short**: preg-only gate vs version-adaptive gate
- **gate-adaptive-1kb**: preg-only gate vs version-adaptive gate
- **tier-strrep**: htmlspecialchars vs gated str_replace tier
- **gate-unicode**: two-tier (bails on UTF-8) vs three-tier (/u pass)
- **gate-hybrid-short**: shipped preg gate vs hybrid-len gate
- **gate-hybrid-1kb**: shipped preg gate vs hybrid-len gate
- **gate-hybrid-mix**: shipped preg gate vs hybrid-len gate
- **scan-cross-10**: preg scan 10B vs strspn scan 10B
- **scan-cross-64**: preg scan 64B vs strspn scan 64B
- **scan-cross-128**: preg scan 128B vs strspn scan 128B
- **scan-cross-256**: preg scan 256B vs strspn scan 256B
- **scan-cross-512**: preg scan 512B vs strspn scan 512B
- **thresh-128-128b**: hybrid gate (256B min) vs hybrid gate (128B min)
- **thresh-128-200b**: hybrid gate (256B min) vs hybrid gate (128B min)
- **cast-int**: cast then tier scan vs is_string fast path
- **cast-guard-short**: tier scan only vs is_string check + tier scan
- **thresh-64-64b**: hybrid gate (128B min) vs hybrid gate (64B min)
- **thresh-64-96b**: hybrid gate (128B min) vs hybrid gate (64B min)
- **thresh-os-64b**: hybrid gate (128B min) vs OS-gated 64B min (const-folded)
- **thresh-arch-64b**: hybrid gate (128B min) vs arch-gated 64B min (runtime const)
- **thresh-arch-short**: hybrid gate (128B min) vs arch-gated 64B min (runtime const)
- **strtr-sparse-1kb**: str_replace tier vs strtr tier
- **strtr-dense-1kb**: str_replace tier vs strtr tier
- **strtr-short**: str_replace tier vs strtr tier
- **tier-os-gated-short**: ungated two-tier vs OS-gated two-tier
- **tier-os-gated-dirty**: ungated two-tier vs OS-gated two-tier
- **stack-mix**: htmlspecialchars vs three-tier stacked
- **stack-accented-mix**: htmlspecialchars vs three-tier stacked
- **stack-miss-short**: htmlspecialchars vs three-tier stacked
- **stack-accented-short**: htmlspecialchars vs three-tier stacked
- **stack-invalid-1kb**: htmlspecialchars vs three-tier stacked
- **arr-get**: current 3-call chain vs folded single-lookup __get
- **arr-get-mixed**: tuned, union return vs tuned, mixed return
- **no-object**: object + __toString vs direct encoded string
- **arr-get-method**: ->get(key) full chain vs ->key folded __get
- **arr-foreach**: generator getIterator vs ArrayIterator over rows
- **idiom**: (string) cast vs ->htmlEncode()
- **memo-mix**: gate only vs gate + memo cache

</details>
